title: Managing Risk on a Lesson
whatItIs: Risk management is the second marked area on part 3 and the standards check, with 5 competences. Scoring 7 or less in it is an automatic fail, whatever the total.
keyFacts: The instructor is always responsible for their own safety, the pupil's and other road users'.
Make sure the pupil understands how responsibility for risk is shared, and keep managing it all lesson.
Explain when and how you may use verbal or physical interventions to keep everyone safe.
Give clear instructions in good time; late, confusing or too many directions add risk.
Be fit to teach, check the learner is fit to start, and take suitable action if not.

rows: Pupil knows who does what, incl. dual controls
Watches the road and the pupil
Steps in only when the pupil can't cope
Pupil helped to understand what happened

a.label: Early learner, dual-control car
points: Instructor may take control in an emergency
Then you talk about what happened

b.label: Full licence holder, own car
points: Instructor stays quiet but flags missed risks

onTheTest.question: On a part 3 test a PDI scores 38 in total, but only 7 in the risk management section. What is the result?
options: Pass, with risk management to be retested
onTheTest.why: GOV.UK part 3 test: you automatically fail if you score 7 or less in the risk management category, whatever your total score.

onTheTest.question: Under the training standard, what should an instructor do when they spot a hazard the learner doesn't seem aware of?
options: Wait and discuss it at the end
Say nothing so the learner learns
Note it for the next lesson
onTheTest.why: Element 6.4.1: take suitable and timely action where you identify a hazard the learner doesn't appear to be aware of, then use client-centred techniques so they cope better in future.

traps: Intervening when the pupil is coping is also a fault, not just failing to step in.
Silence can be a coaching input: it can show the pupil you're confident in them.
As a supervising driver you're in control: no mobile phone and no alcohol, as if driving.
